clue.text: Philosopher saved in a dangerous situation

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., the English philosopher and statesman
the idiom 'save one's ...' means to rescue oneself from danger, so this is what gets saved

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the idiom 'save one's bacon': the word is what is saved when you get out of a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Elizabethan thinker Francis Bacon; the other is the thing rescued in the idiom about escaping peril.

clue.text: No rise for those more advanced in service

indicators.note: for here is read as 'in exchange for', the letters of the phrase traded for a new order

parts.note: the six letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff complain there is no pay rise for long-serving employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a very loose anagram signal: rearrange the letters of NO RISE. 'those' is padding that makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone higher in rank or longer in post is the elder or higher-ranking one in a workplace.

clue.text: How slowly one travelled in olden days

definitions.text: How slowly one travelled in olden days

parts.words: How slowly one travelled in olden days
parts.note: a coach journey was made in legs between posting inns, which also gives the phrase meaning gradually

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, and literally describes a stagecoach trip made leg by leg.

clue.text: Sense men gain in reformation

indicators.note: reformation means forming again, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men find sense in a religious reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: The sense of a word is its significance or import.

clue.text: This poem is about the devil

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a poem concerns Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the eight letters of THIS POEM. Mephistopheles is the devil of the Faust legend, the subject of famous poetic dramas, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Mephistopheles, the demon to whom Faust sells his soul.

clue.text: Music said to get in the dough

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rolling pasta works it into a sheet of dough, so this phrase gives 'pasta roll'

explanation.surface: Someone claims music is a way of getting rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get in the dough' looks like slang for making money, but it leads to 'pasta roll', which spoken aloud gives the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a piece of music evoking rural life, a type of composition.

clue.text: It may catch one in the act

definitions.text: It may catch one in the act

parts.words: It may catch one in the act
parts.note: the act is a circus trapeze performance, and the mesh below catches a falling performer, not a criminal

explanation.definitionFit: A mesh slung beneath acrobats to break a fall is a safeguard in a circus.

clue.text: Four-legged race?

parts.note: not a horse race but a team race run in four stages or legs by four runners

explanation.definitionFit: A team running event is divided into legs, usually four, with a baton passed between runners.

clue.text: Raise the stake for mount hotly tipped when it runs

definitions.text: mount hotly tipped when it runs

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler ups the bet on a horse that is the hot favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about betting on a fancied horse, but the mount is a mountain whose hot top erupts with running lava.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a mountain whose summit glows when lava flows.

clue.text: Where water speed records were set-not sonic however

definitions.text: Where water speed records were set

indicators.note: however here means 'in whatever way', so the letters may be arranged in any way

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Speedboat records were set on a lake, though not at supersonic speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Coniston Water is a lake in the English Lake District where Malcolm and Donald Campbell set water speed records.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District lake is famous for Campbell's record-breaking speedboat runs.

clue.text: It hit a Pacific island badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something struck an island in the Pacific hard, perhaps a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of French Polynesia lies in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Note arrangement of sails and masts of a vessel

parts.note: B is a musical note
a ship's rig is its arrangement of masts and sails

explanation.surface: A sailor notes how the sails and masts of a ship are set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted square-rigged sailing ship is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Company that was floated to avoid liquidation

definitions.text: Company that was floated to avoid liquidation

parts.words: Company that was floated to avoid liquidation
parts.note: not a business floated on the stock market to stave off bankruptcy, but a boatload of animals launched to escape drowning in the Flood

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical vessel carried a company of creatures afloat through the Flood, escaping the waters.

clue.text: House plot developed with only northern views?

indicators.note: a plot that is developed is built upon and changed, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A building plot is developed so that its houses face only north.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the place rather than naming it: from the planet's southernmost point every direction is north.
explanation.definitionFit: At the bottom of the globe, any way you look is toward the north.

clue.text: Trick examination question

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A trick question appears on an exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or challenge something is to question it.

clue.text: Snuggled into new quilt, managed to remain undisturbed

indicators.note: something snuggled into a covering is tucked inside it
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of the word quilt

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: Someone snuggled into a new quilt and managed to lie peacefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for the quilt alone; 'Snuggled into' tells you the managed word goes inside that rearrangement, so the surface's cosy sleeper is a container picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and peaceful means not troubled or agitated.

clue.text: Makes slow progress by street-car

parts.note: Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, the British luxury car

explanation.surface: Traffic crawls along, as if by streetcar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street-car' looks like one word (a tram) but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking at a leisurely pace means moving along unhurriedly.

clue.text: Its report is deliberately delayed

parts.note: report means a bang, the explosion that comes only when a timer runs out

explanation.definitionFit: An explosive device fitted with a timer goes off at a set later moment.

clue.text: One of nine in plot is perplexed

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A conspirator is baffled by one of nine schemers in a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy but is a flower bed; the nine are the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puzzled or bewildered is a synonym for confused.

clue.text: Take an attitude over something that's beneath you

definitions.text: Take an attitude over something that's beneath you

parts.words: Take an attitude over something that's beneath you
parts.note: not a snobbish stance, but literally standing with legs either side of something below

explanation.definitionFit: To sit or stand with legs on each side of something is to bestride it.

clue.text: Becomes stiff

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, so becoming one means passing away

explanation.definitionFit: Passing away turns a person into a corpse, slang 'stiff'.

clue.text: Cleans up after many short operations

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A hospital cleaner tidies up after a run of brief surgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping a floor with a wet head on a stick is cleaning it.

clue.text: Promise to drink one's health

definitions.meaning: an old sense meaning to toast someone

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a solemn vow and, in an older sense, a toast raised to someone.

clue.text: A pound to one the hermit will be

parts.note: L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra
taken as written

explanation.surface: Betting odds of a pound to one are offered on how a recluse will end up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like betting odds, but 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives by himself, solitary and without company.

clue.text: Pop a question that's somewhat obscure

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: Someone pops the question in a rather vague way.
explanation.definitionFit: Not clear or transparent, hard to understand or see through.

clue.text: It gets held up when the weather's bad

definitions.text: It gets held up when the weather's bad

parts.words: It gets held up when the weather's bad
parts.note: not something delayed by storms but something raised overhead against rain

explanation.definitionFit: A folding canopy on a stick is raised above the head in rain.

clue.text: Instinct for money in the market

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fair is a market
L is the abbreviation for a pound, money

explanation.surface: Someone has an instinct for making money in the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the stock market; here a market is a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or knack is an innate aptitude.

clue.text: She makes man target

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman makes a man her target.
explanation.walkthrough: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, so the man is her target.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a shrewish woman, so 'she' stands for her.
